note: The eight sites of the Memorials gallery. Each entry drives (a) a plinth on the map table, (b) a stylised walk-through reconstruction generated by the world builder, and (c) an information panel with narration. Every reconstruction is labelled 'Digital Reconstruction' in-scene; the models are built from public descriptions of the sites and are not surveyed.
reconstructionLabel: Digital Reconstruction — artistic visualisation built from public descriptions of the site. Not a surveyed model and not an authentic photograph.

sites.name: Bhim Janmabhoomi

tour.label: The approach
tour.text: The birthplace is marked by a memorial and a public library in the town where the family lived while his father served in the cantonment.

tour.label: The memorial garden
tour.text: The garden is laid out for the annual observances on 14 April, when the site is visited by large numbers of people.

tour.label: The library
tour.text: A reading room stands beside the memorial: the education theme of the movement, made into a building on the site of the birth.

sites.narration: Mhow, 14 April 1891. A cantonment town, an army family, and a child born into a community that would be excluded from the schools and wells around it.

sites.name: Rajgruha — the Dadar residence

tour.label: The street
tour.text: Hindu Colony, Dadar: the house he built in the 1930s and lived in with his family for two decades.

tour.label: The library
tour.text: The working library is the centre of the reconstruction: shelves, a reading chair, and a desk with the marks of a working scholar's room.

tour.label: The museum rooms
tour.text: The house is maintained as a memorial and museum, holding his books and personal effects.

sites.narration: A scholar's house is mostly a library with rooms attached. At Dadar, the collection is the building.

sites.name: Chaitya Bhoomi

tour.label: The seafront approach
tour.text: The memorial stands at Dadar Chowpatty, on the shoreline, where the cremation took place on 7 December 1956.

tour.label: The memorial canopy
tour.text: The reconstructed canopy and stepped platform are shown as an architectural reconstruction, not a measured survey of the existing structure.

tour.label: 6 December
tour.text: The site is the focus of the largest annual observances, especially on 6 December and during the October Dhamma Chakra Pravartan Din.

sites.narration: The largest memorial in this archive is also the youngest: a shoreline site that became a place of national remembrance within a single generation.

sites.name: Deekshabhoomi

tour.label: The approach
tour.text: The grounds at Nagpur where, on 14 October 1956, the conversion ceremony took place before a very large gathering.

tour.label: The stupa
tour.text: A hemispherical stupa now stands on the site, consecrated in 2001. The reconstruction simplifies its geometry and is labelled as a reconstruction.

tour.label: Dhamma Chakra Pravartan Din
tour.text: The annual October observance returns to this ground, closing the loop between the conversion and the writing of 'The Buddha and His Dhamma'.

sites.narration: On 14 October 1956, the refuges and the five precepts were taken, and twenty-two vows administered, in an open ground at Nagpur.

sites.name: Dr. Ambedkar National Memorial

tour.label: The house
tour.text: 26 Alipur Road, Delhi: the residence of his last years, in which he died on 6 December 1956.

tour.label: The study
tour.text: The reconstruction includes a study with a desk and manuscript table, where work on 'The Buddha and His Dhamma' continued into his last weeks.

tour.label: The national memorial
tour.text: Developed as a national memorial and inaugurated on 14 April 2018 under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

sites.narration: Six weeks after Nagpur, in a house on Alipur Road in Delhi, the last manuscript was left unfinished.

sites.name: Ambedkar Memorial Park

tour.label: The colonnade
tour.text: Long sandstone colonnades frame a central axis, in a monumental idiom drawn from Buddhist and Indian architectural traditions.

tour.label: The water channel
tour.text: Reflecting water runs the length of the axis; the reconstruction greatly simplifies the planting and the stonework detail.

tour.label: The central stupa
tour.text: A central stupa and memorial walls carry the names of figures of the social-reform tradition, not only Dr. Ambedkar.

sites.narration: A public park remembers a movement as well as a person: the colonnade carries more than one name.

sites.name: Statue on the Hussain Sagar lakefront

tour.label: The lakefront
tour.text: The statue stands on the Hussain Sagar lakefront, unveiled on 14 April 2016.

tour.label: The monument
tour.text: The figure is shown as a silhouette in this reconstruction. The platform does not reproduce a likeness in monumental form: the character model in the museum is the labelled avatar, and monuments are represented by their structure.

tour.label: Scale
tour.text: At this scale the monument is a landmark for a whole city, which is a different kind of memory from a house or a library.

sites.narration: Not every memorial is a building. Some are a scale: a figure visible from across a lake.

sites.name: Dr. Ambedkar International Centre

tour.label: The atrium
tour.text: A research and documentation institution on Janpath in New Delhi, with reading rooms and a public programme.

tour.label: The reading room
tour.text: This is the part of the gallery that resembles the platform itself: a place designed for study rather than display.

tour.label: The institution's role
tour.text: The Centre is the natural host for a digital archive of this kind: it already holds, catalogues and publishes the material.

sites.narration: The last site in the gallery is not about the past at all. It is about who keeps the record open.
